# Introduction

Motivate the method: Which problem does it solve, and where is it used? State the goal of your thesis and give an overview of its structure.

# Assumptions

State the statistical model and all assumptions under which the method is justified. Explain what each assumption means and where it is needed.

# How the Method Works

Define the method formally, give the intuition behind it, and state its main theoretical properties. Cite your sources, e.g., @Silverman1986.

Show code only when it helps the reader to understand the method, and keep such snippets short:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
ci_mean <- function(x, level = 0.95) {
  q <- qt(1 - (1 - level) / 2, df = length(x) - 1)
  mean(x) + c(-1, 1) * q * sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
}
```

# Application

Apply the method to a (real or simulated) data example and interpret the results.

# Simulation Study

Describe the design of your simulation study: the data generating processes, which assumption each of them violates, the sample sizes, the number of replications, and the performance measures.

The following example studies the coverage probability of the classical 95% confidence interval for the mean, which assumes normally distributed data. @tbl-coverage and @fig-coverage show the results based on `r sim$B` Monte Carlo replications.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Empirical coverage probabilities of the 95% confidence interval for the mean."
tab <- reshape(sim$results, idvar = "dgp", timevar = "n", direction = "wide")
names(tab) <- c("Distribution", paste0("n = ", unique(sim$results$n)))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Empirical coverage probabilities. The dashed line marks the nominal level of 95%."
res <- sim$results
plot(NULL, xlim = range(res$n), ylim = c(min(res$coverage, 0.85), 1),
     log = "x", xlab = "Sample size n", ylab = "Coverage probability")
abline(h = 0.95, lty = 2)
for (i in seq_along(unique(res$dgp))) {
  d <- res[res$dgp == unique(res$dgp)[i], ]
  lines(d$n, d$coverage, type = "b", pch = i, lty = 1)
}
legend("bottomright", legend = unique(res$dgp), pch = seq_along(unique(res$dgp)),
       bty = "n")
```

Interpret the results: When can a user rely on the method? What should a user watch out for in practice?
